title: Mary Shelley and the Mother She Never Knew
text:
Mary Wollstonecraft, author of A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, married the philosopher William Godwin in March 1797, when she was already expecting their child. On 30 August she gave birth to a daughter, Mary. The placenta did not come away properly, infection set in, and on 10 September 1797 Wollstonecraft died. Her daughter was eleven days old.

Godwin, grieving, wrote a frank memoir of his wife's life, including her love affairs and suicide attempts. It shocked the public and damaged her reputation for a century. He raised Mary and her older half-sister Fanny, and later remarried.

Mary grew up surrounded by her mother's books and legend. She read and reread her writings. Wollstonecraft was buried in the churchyard of St Pancras in London, and Mary went there often. Biographers record that she read and studied by her mother's grave. In 1814, at sixteen, it was there that she met in secret with the young poet Percy Bysshe Shelley, a disciple of her father. In July 1814 they ran away together to the continent, against her father's furious objections.

Four years later, in 1818, Mary Shelley published Frankenstein, a novel about a creature brought into the world and abandoned by its maker. Later she became the editor and keeper of Shelley's work. Her mother, whom she never knew, remained her guide.
lesson: A parent we never knew can still shape us through what she left behind. What we write and believe may become a child's inheritance.
people: Mary Wollstonecraft, Mary Shelley, William Godwin, Percy Bysshe Shelley
source: William Godwin, Memoirs of the Author of A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1798); Miranda Seymour, Mary Shelley (2000)
